newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban said to take northeastern town.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban said to take northeastern town.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic Taleban militia on Wednesday captured the northeastern town of Taloqan, headquarters of ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service said.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said the purist Islamic militia had seized Taloqan, capital of Takhar province, with the help of local commanders and local people after an overnight offensive from neighbouring Kunduz province.

It said Afghan opposition sources in the Pakistani border town of Peshawar had confirmed the fall of Taloqan, which Rabbani and Ittehad-i-Islami chief Abdurrab Rasul Sayyaf had used as a temporary base since the Taleban drove the Rabbani government from Kabul in September.

AIP said the Taleban, which controls more than two-thirds of Afghanistan, including the capital Kabul, had launched a major offensive into Takhar province from Kunduz on Tuesday evening, killing 20 soldiers loyal to former government commander Ahmed Shah Masood and capturing 285 after intense fighting. The Taleban lost eight dead.
AIP said two helicopters had taken off from Taloqan for an undisclosed destination on Tuesday, apparently with opposition leaders on board, but it could not identify them.

Earlier, the Taleban attackers broke through opposition frontlines and thrust into Khwaja Ghar and Bangi districts, about 30 km (19 miles) west of Taloqan. The militia earlier captured the Qabr-i-Qazi district, east of Kunduz, AIP said.
AIP said local commanders had joined the Taleban offensive, swelling the militia's ranks to 1,500 from an initial 1,000.
